record.original_question: Does there exist a singular measure in Zygmund’s class A∗ all of whose Fourier-Stieltjes coefficients are non-negative? (F. Holland)

evidence.quote: Does there exist a singular measure in Zygmund’s class A∗ all of whose Fourier-Stieltjes coefficients are non-negative? (F. Holland)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$ denote the unit circle. Zygmund's class $\Lambda_*$ (also denoted $A_*$) consists of all continuous functions $f: \mathbb{T} \to \mathbb{C}$ satisfying the smoothness condition
$$\sup_{x\in\mathbb{T},\, h>0} \frac{|f(x+h) + f(x-h) - 2f(x)|}{h} < \infty.$$
A finite complex Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{T}$ is said to belong to $\Lambda_*$ if its indefinite integral $F(x) = \mu([0,x])$ belongs to $\Lambda_*$, equivalently if there is a constant $C$ such that $|\mu(I)| \le C\,|I|$ for every arc $I \subset \mathbb{T}$ and the appropriate symmetric second-difference condition holds. The Fourier–Stieltjes coefficients of $\mu$ are
$$\hat{\mu}(n) = \int_{\mathbb{T}} e^{-in\theta}\, d\mu(\theta), \qquad n \in \mathbb{Z}.$$
A measure $\mu$ is called singular if it is singular with respect to Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{T}$.

Question: Does there exist a singular (finite, positive or signed) measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{T}$ belonging to Zygmund's class $\Lambda_*$ such that $\hat{\mu}(n) \ge 0$ for every $n \in \mathbb{Z}$?
